quests.instruction: Lina has 20 minutes before leaving for school. Getting dressed takes 5 minutes, breakfast takes 10 and packing her bag takes 5. Which statement is correct?
quests.correctAnswer: She Has Just Enough Time for All Three ✅
options: She Has Time to Add a Long Game as Well 🎮
She Must Skip Breakfast Because Time Is Short 🥣
She Has Just Enough Time for All Three ✅
quests.hint: Add up the minutes and compare them with the 20 she has.
quests.explanation: Five plus ten plus five is twenty minutes, which matches the time she has, so she can do all three if she starts now and does not waste any. There is no room for a long game.
quests.funFact: The abacus, used for adding numbers, was in use in ancient Mesopotamia, China and Rome.

quests.instruction: Dev has 15 minutes before the bus. Washing and dressing take 8 minutes, and a full breakfast takes 10. What is the best plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Wash, Dress and Take a Quick Breakfast 🍞
options: Do Everything at Full Length and Miss the Bus 🚌
Skip Washing and Dressing and Eat Breakfast 🥣
Wash, Dress and Take a Quick Breakfast 🍞
quests.hint: Add the two jobs together, then see what fits in 15.
quests.explanation: Eight plus ten is eighteen minutes, which is too long. Shortening the breakfast fits the time and still covers every job.
quests.funFact: Bananas, boiled eggs and nuts are quick breakfast foods that need no cooking.

quests.instruction: Mina has 30 minutes before dinner. Homework takes 20 minutes and tidying her room takes 15. What is a sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Do Homework First and Tidy Up Later 📚
options: Tidy First and Skip Homework Tonight 🧹
Do Homework First and Tidy Up Later 📚
Do Both at the Same Time Somehow 🤹
quests.hint: Add the times, and think about which job has a deadline.
quests.explanation: Twenty plus fifteen is thirty-five minutes, which is five too many. Homework is due, so it comes first and the tidying can wait.
quests.funFact: The Pomodoro technique uses 25-minute work blocks followed by short breaks.

quests.instruction: Before printing homework, Rohan has switched on the printer. What else must he check so that it works?
quests.correctAnswer: There Is Paper in the Tray 🖨️
options: The Printer Is Facing the Window 🪟
His Pencil Case Is Open ✏️
There Is Paper in the Tray 🖨️
quests.hint: Ask yourself what a printer needs besides power.
quests.explanation: A printer needs both power and paper before it can print. Where it faces and whether the pencil case is open make no difference.
quests.funFact: Inkjet printers spray tiny drops of ink onto paper, so the paper has to be in place first.

quests.instruction: Zoya must give her teacher a signed form and a fee in an envelope. Which things must be ready before she leaves home?
quests.correctAnswer: The Signed Form and the Fee 📝
options: The Signed Form and the Fee 📝
The Signed Form on Its Own 🖊️
The Money for the Fee Only 💰
quests.hint: Count how many things the teacher asked for.
quests.explanation: The teacher asked for both, so both must be ready. Taking only one would leave the job unfinished.
quests.funFact: Schools often ask for forms and money together so that one envelope can be handled at once.

quests.instruction: Hari can go out to play once his homework is done and Mum knows. He has finished his homework and put his shoes on. What is left?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell Mum 🗣️
options: Tell Mum 🗣️
Take His Shoes Off 👟
Do His Homework Again 📚
quests.hint: Look back at the two conditions and tick off what is finished.
quests.explanation: The two conditions were homework and telling Mum. Homework is done, so telling Mum is the last step. Shoes are not part of the rule.
quests.funFact: Computers use 'AND' conditions too: a program may run only when two things are both true.

quests.instruction: It is ten minutes before the bus. Ravi has not eaten, packed his bag or combed his hair. Which job can he skip if time runs out?
quests.correctAnswer: Combing His Hair 🪮
options: Packing His Bag 🎒
Eating Something 🍞
Combing His Hair 🪮
quests.hint: The clue is which job matters least for the school day.
quests.explanation: A packed bag and some food are needed for the day, while hair can be neatened later or just left. When time is short, the necessary jobs come first.
quests.funFact: Packing lists for expeditions separate 'essential' items from 'nice to have' ones to save weight.

quests.instruction: At bedtime, Mina is very sleepy. She has to brush her teeth, put on pajamas, tidy her toys and read a story. If she must skip one, which should it be?
quests.correctAnswer: Tidying Her Toys 🧩
options: Putting on Her Pajamas 🧸
Brushing Her Teeth 🪥
Tidying Her Toys 🧩
quests.hint: Decide which job protects her health or comfort for the night.
quests.explanation: Brushing teeth and wearing sleepwear look after her body and comfort, while toys can be tidied tomorrow. The story is a nice extra too, but tidying is the best one to leave.
quests.funFact: Teeth brushed at night help protect against cavities, because the mouth makes less saliva during sleep.

quests.instruction: Leo is packing for a school trip, and time is short. His list: water bottle, packed lunch, hat and toy robot. Which can be left behind?
quests.correctAnswer: The Toy Robot 🤖
options: The Packed Lunch 🍱
The Toy Robot 🤖
The Water Bottle 💧
quests.hint: The clue is what he will need during the day.
quests.explanation: Water, lunch and a hat are needed for a day out, but a toy is just for fun. When time is short, only essentials go in.
quests.funFact: Trip lists from schools often separate 'must bring' items from 'please do not bring' items such as toys.

quests.instruction: Dia must wash her hands, set the table and serve the rice. She must wash her hands before touching food, and the table must be set before the rice is served. Which order works?
quests.correctAnswer: Wash Hands, Set the Table, Serve the Rice 🍚
options: Serve the Rice, Wash Hands, Set the Table 🍽️
Wash Hands, Set the Table, Serve the Rice 🍚
Set the Table, Serve the Rice, Wash Hands 🧼
quests.hint: Check each order against both rules.
quests.explanation: Washing hands comes before touching food, and setting the table comes before serving. Only one order obeys both.
quests.funFact: A recipe is a set of instructions in which the order of steps matters, such as creaming butter before adding flour.

quests.instruction: Rain is expected in thirty minutes, and Rohan has three jobs: take out the rubbish, finish his homework and bring in the washing. Which job is the most urgent?
quests.correctAnswer: Bringing In the Washing 🧺
options: Bringing In the Washing 🧺
Finishing His Homework 📝
Taking Out the Rubbish 🗑️
quests.hint: Remember which job gets worse if it waits for the rain.
quests.explanation: Washing left outside will get wet, but the rubbish and homework can wait a little. The job with a time limit comes first.
quests.funFact: Forecasts of rain are often updated through the day, so checking again before leaving is sensible.

quests.instruction: Rice is cooking on the stove and will take twenty minutes. Which jobs can Aman do while it cooks?
quests.correctAnswer: Set the Table and Wash Up Other Dishes 🍽️
options: Stand Close to the Hot Pan to Watch 🔥
Set the Table and Wash Up Other Dishes 🍽️
Lift the Lid to Check the Rice Often 🍚
quests.hint: Consider useful jobs that are away from the heat.
quests.explanation: Setting the table and washing up use the waiting time well, and keep him away from the hot pan. Lifting the lid often slows the cooking and standing close is unsafe.
quests.funFact: A pressure cooker can cook rice or lentils in a fraction of the usual time.

quests.instruction: A family rule says: 'If it is raining, take an umbrella. If it is sunny, take a hat.' Today is sunny, and Ila's bag is packed. What else should she take?
quests.correctAnswer: A Hat 🧢
options: A Raincoat 🧥
A Hat 🧢
An Umbrella ☂️
quests.hint: Check which condition is true today.
quests.explanation: The rule gives a hat for sunny days, and today is sunny. The umbrella and raincoat are for rain.
quests.funFact: Rules of the form 'if this, then that' are the basis of many instructions, from recipes to computer programs.

quests.instruction: The house rule is: shoes off at the door, then bag in the hallway, then hands washed before a snack. Anu has taken her shoes off. What is next?
quests.correctAnswer: Put Her Bag in the Hallway 🎒
options: Put Her Bag in the Hallway 🎒
Eat the Snack Straight Away 🍎
Wash Her Hands at the Sink 💧
quests.hint: Follow the order of the rule one step at a time.
quests.explanation: After shoes comes the bag, then hands, then the snack. Washing hands or eating now would skip a step.
quests.funFact: Recipes, board-game rules and computer programs are all lists of steps that must be followed in order.

quests.instruction: The rule is: 'If homework is finished, screen time is allowed for thirty minutes. If not, none.' Dev has finished maths but not reading. What can he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Finish Reading First, Then Screen Time 📖
options: Skip Reading and Hope Nobody Notices 🙈
Start Screen Time Now 📱
Finish Reading First, Then Screen Time 📖
quests.hint: Check whether the condition in the rule has been met.
quests.explanation: Homework is not finished until reading is done, so the condition is not yet true. Finishing reading meets the rule, and then screen time is allowed.
quests.funFact: In rules with a condition, nothing happens until the condition is met.

quests.instruction: The bus leaves at 8:00 and Meera needs 10 minutes to walk to the stop. What is the latest time she should leave home?
quests.hint: Count back ten minutes from eight o'clock.
quests.explanation: Ten minutes before 8:00 is 7:50. Leaving at 8:00 or later would mean she misses the bus.
quests.funFact: A rocket launch uses a countdown that counts backwards from ten to zero.

quests.instruction: Dinner is at 7:00 and Aman's homework takes 30 minutes. What is the latest sensible time to start it?
quests.hint: Count back thirty minutes from seven.
quests.explanation: Thirty minutes before 7:00 is 6:30. Starting later would run into dinner.
quests.funFact: A stopwatch can count up or down, which is how many people time their jobs.

quests.instruction: A film starts at 4:00. It takes 20 minutes to get to the cinema and 10 minutes to buy tickets. When should the family leave?
quests.hint: Add the two times together, then count back from four.
quests.explanation: Twenty plus ten is thirty minutes, so leaving at 3:30 gets them there for the start. Later times would make them late.
quests.funFact: Booking cinema tickets in advance often lets you choose your seats.

quests.instruction: Ira is late for school. She can walk the safe path in 20 minutes or take a shortcut across a busy road in 10. Which is the better choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Walk the Safe Path and Tell the Teacher 🚶
options: Take the Shortcut Across the Busy Road 🚗
Skip School Because She Is Late 🏠
Walk the Safe Path and Tell the Teacher 🚶
quests.hint: Remember what matters more than saving ten minutes.
quests.explanation: Safety matters more than speed, and the teacher can be told why she is late. Crossing a busy road in a hurry is risky, and skipping school is not needed.
quests.funFact: The zebra crossing is named after the black-and-white stripes of a zebra.

quests.instruction: Mina's bag is heavy, and she can carry only some books home. Her homework book is needed tonight, her library book is due next week and her art kit is not needed until Friday. Which should she carry home?
quests.correctAnswer: The Homework Book 📚
options: The Art Kit 🎨
The Library Book 📖
The Homework Book 📚
quests.hint: Think about which is needed soonest.
quests.explanation: The homework book is needed tonight. The others can stay at school for now because they are not needed until later.
quests.funFact: A school bag with chest and waist straps spreads the weight across the body.

quests.instruction: Rohan's tablet is at 20 per cent, and he needs it for homework in thirty minutes. What is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Plug It In and Use It While Charging 🔌
options: Plug It In and Use It While Charging 🔌
Wait Three Hours for a Full Charge 🕒
Use It Until It Dies, Then Worry 😰
quests.hint: Work out how to have power when he needs it.
quests.explanation: Plugging in gives power while he works. Waiting three hours or running out of power would stop his homework.
quests.funFact: Most tablets can be used while charging, and a short charge can add a lot of battery.

quests.instruction: A note on the table says: 'Back at 5. Snacks are in the green box. Homework before TV.' What is Joy's plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Snack, Then Homework, Then TV 🍎
options: Homework, Then Wait Until Mum Gets Back 🕰️
Snack, Then Homework, Then TV 🍎
TV, Then Snack, Then Homework 📺
quests.hint: Pick out each instruction in the note and put them in order.
quests.explanation: The note says snacks are available and that homework comes before TV. So she has a snack, does homework and then watches TV.
quests.funFact: A highlighter pen has see-through ink, so the words underneath can still be read.

quests.instruction: A school notice says: 'PE kit on Tuesday, library book on Thursday, swimming bag on Friday.' What does Mina need on Thursday?
quests.correctAnswer: A Library Book 📚
options: A Library Book 📚
A PE Kit 👟
A Swimming Bag 🏊
quests.hint: Find Thursday in the notice.
quests.explanation: The notice pairs each day with one thing, and Thursday goes with the library book. The others belong to other days.
quests.funFact: A weekly timetable stuck on the fridge makes it easy to see what to bring each day.

quests.instruction: A note says: 'Wash up, then dry, then put away. Do not use the green towel.' What should Aman do with the green towel?
quests.correctAnswer: Leave It Alone 🚫
options: Wrap the Wet Plates in It 🧣
Use It to Dry the Plates 🍽️
Leave It Alone 🚫
quests.hint: Look for the part of the note about the green towel.
quests.explanation: The note says not to use it, so he leaves it alone and uses another towel. Using it would ignore the instruction.
quests.funFact: Warnings such as 'do not' stand out more when they are written in bold or capital letters.

quests.instruction: Rohan stays up late, so he wakes up tired, so he rushes breakfast and forgets his bag. Which earlier choice would have prevented the whole chain?
quests.correctAnswer: Going to Bed on Time 🌙
options: Going to Bed on Time 🌙
Eating Breakfast Even Faster 🥣
Waking Up Earlier Still ⏰
quests.hint: Look for the very first link in the chain.
quests.explanation: Going to bed on time stops the chain at its start, since he would wake rested and not rush. Fixing later links only treats the symptoms.
quests.funFact: The 'domino effect' describes one small event setting off a chain of others, like a line of falling dominoes.

quests.instruction: A glass is left near the edge of the table, it is bumped, it spills, and then someone slips on the wet floor. Which step would prevent the problem best?
quests.correctAnswer: Put the Glass Away from the Edge 🥛
options: Put the Glass Away from the Edge 🥛
Mop the Floor After Someone Slips 🧽
Run Past the Table Quickly 🏃
quests.hint: Consider stopping the problem before it begins.
quests.explanation: Moving the glass stops the chain at the start. Mopping after someone slips comes too late, and running past makes bumps more likely.
quests.funFact: Hospitals use non-slip floors and handrails to remove hazards before accidents happen.

quests.instruction: The bag was not packed, a book was forgotten, the homework could not be shown, and the teacher was upset. What would break the chain earliest?
quests.correctAnswer: Packing the Bag the Evening Before 🎒
options: Explaining to the Teacher Later 🗣️
Copying a Friend's Work 📋
Packing the Bag the Evening Before 🎒
quests.hint: Find the first thing that went wrong.
quests.explanation: Packing the evening before stops the chain at its first step. Explaining afterwards or copying deals with the effects, not the cause.
quests.funFact: A cause that happens early in a chain is called a root cause.

quests.instruction: Dev has 25 minutes before bed. A shower takes 10 minutes, dinner takes 15 and homework takes 20. Which pair can he finish in that time?
quests.correctAnswer: Shower and Dinner 🍲
options: Dinner and Homework 📚
Shower and Dinner 🍲
Shower and Homework 📝
quests.hint: Add each pair of times and compare with 25.
quests.explanation: Ten plus fifteen is 25, which fits. Shower and homework is 30, and dinner and homework is 35, which are too long.
quests.funFact: Adding numbers in tens is easier, such as 10 + 15 = 25.

quests.instruction: Two jobs are waiting: the milk has been left on the counter and the muddy shoes need soaking. Which should be done first?
quests.correctAnswer: Put the Milk in the Fridge 🥛
options: Put the Milk in the Fridge 🥛
Tidy the Whole Bookshelf Up 📚
Soak the Muddy Shoes in Water 👟
quests.hint: Think about which one gets worse quickly.
quests.explanation: Milk can spoil when it is left warm, so the fridge comes first. Shoes and the bookshelf can wait a little.
quests.funFact: Milk is usually kept in the fridge because warm temperatures help germs grow.

quests.instruction: Which is the best way to plan a busy afternoon with three jobs?
quests.correctAnswer: List Jobs, Estimate Times, Do Urgent Ones First 📋
options: Wait for Someone Else to Tell Her What to Do Next 🕰️
List Jobs, Estimate Times, Do Urgent Ones First 📋
Start with Whatever Job Looks the Easiest 🧩
quests.hint: Decide how to see the whole afternoon at once.
quests.explanation: A list with estimated times shows what fits and what is urgent. Doing the easiest first or waiting for orders leaves things to chance.
quests.funFact: Project planners use Gantt charts to show tasks and how long each one takes.
